Hi team,

As part of our SIG/SOC2 internal review, InfoSec needs concrete BCP/DR evidence from vendors that support custody of critical models and inference traffic. Specifically for Redwood:

- Documented RTO and RPO commitments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes (we understand these vary by offering — please indicate which numbers apply to which mode).

- The runbook excerpts describing warm-cache and state replication steps for multi-region failover.
- Any scheduled windows or limitations we should be aware of (KV cache priming times, etc.).

Can you provide the artifacts or point us to a secure folder? Our external audit window opens 2026-11-30 — would appreciate these by 2026-11-20 to give our auditors time.

Thanks,
Mike Rivera
Senior InfoSec Manager
Silverline Financial

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear list. Apologies for the short turnaround; attaching the artifacts requested. Brief summary below and links to the secure folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEXAMPLElink (access granted to Silverline auditors).

Quick answers:
- RTO / RPO by offering (summary):
  • Hosted API: operational RTO observed ~5 minutes in our exercises for stateless endpoints; RPO effectively 0 for stateless inference (no persistent writes).
  • Dedicated (reserved capacity): we measure median RTO ~2 minutes when reserved pools are available; RPO 0 for inference streams; for stateful customer-managed stores RPO depends on replication settings (we documented caveats in the CSV).
  • Private (VPC/on-prem): RTO/RPO are customer-dependent — we provide runbook and best-practice targets (see runbook extract).

- What we attached: redwood_ops_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook excerpts, KV priming steps), failover_test_trace_20261110.log (raw trace + one-pager summary), kv_warmup_snapshot_20261110.json (token priming trace), rto_rpo_matrix_2026Q3.csv (SLA and observed metrics).

- Observed constraints: cold-to-warm cache priming adds ~3 minutes to recovery for cached model paths; DNS TTLs and CDN edge convergence are the primary variable factors for external client-visible RTO. We call this out in the runbook.

Next steps:
- If Silverline auditors want a live witness (short guided replay) we can schedule a 30–45 minute window prior to 11/30.
- If you need redacted low-level traces or a signed attestation, let me know and we'll route through compliance.

Thanks — Karthik

Attachments: redwood_ops_runbook_v2.pdf; failover_test_trace_20261110.log; kv_warmup_snapshot_20261110.json; rto_rpo_matrix_2026Q3.csv
